around.summary: Inspectors found expired items and stale bread during checks at Bengaluru's 5-star hotels and a hospital kitchen, and the crackdown has now put Dakshina Kannada restaurants on alert too. around.summary: About 1,000 residents turned out to protest the fatal accident on a damaged, unbarricaded road stretch this week, but officials have again only promised a wait rather than a fix. around.summary: Traffic curbs have been announced for August 15, and BMRCL will temporarily close Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Metro Station that day. Plan an alternate route or extra travel time if you're headed anywhere near the city centre for Independence Day.

around.summary: The state cabinet approved a bill restricting events at public spaces, reportedly aimed at curbing RSS-linked gatherings. Worth watching if you're planning to organise or attend any public assembly — permission requirements could tighten.

around.headline: Rapido to cover full medical costs for bedridden Bengaluru rider after accident
around.summary: Rapido has agreed to process full medical costs for a customer left bedridden after a ride accident. It's a reminder that ride-hailing aggregators are required to carry personal accident cover for riders — documenting the accident (driver details, photos, a police complaint) right away is what makes such a claim possible later.

street_smart.title: You're injured in an accident mid-ride on a Rapido/Ola/Uber auto or bike taxi — like today's Bengaluru case where Rapido agreed to cover a rider's full medical costs after they were left bedridden. What do you do right after the accident to make sure that kind of support is actually available to you later?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru news: Rapido agreed to process full medical costs for a customer left bedridden after an accident during a ride (The Times of India).
street_smart.situation: The auto you're riding in is hit and you're hurt, but conscious and able to move around. The driver is apologetic and people are gathering to help.

choices.text: Accept a cash amount the driver offers on the spot to "sort it out quietly" and skip filing anything formal.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. An on-the-spot cash payment feels like a fast resolution, but it leaves you with no documentation, no FIR, and no formal claim — if your injuries turn out worse than they first seemed, you've already given up your ability to claim the aggregator's accident cover or insurance.

choices.text: Note the driver's name and vehicle number, photograph the scene and your injuries, call 108 if needed, file a police complaint, and report the ride through the app's SOS/support within 24 hours.
choices.feedback: Correct. Aggregators like Rapido, Ola and Uber are required to carry personal accident cover for riders, but claiming it depends on documentation created right away — driver and vehicle details, photos, a police complaint, and a timely in-app report are exactly what turned today's case into Rapido agreeing to cover costs.

choices.text: Report the incident through the app's support chat, but skip the police complaint since the driver seems cooperative and apologetic.
choices.feedback: Risky. An in-app report alone is often not enough supporting documentation for an insurance or platform compensation claim — a police complaint or FIR matters regardless of how cooperative the driver seems in the moment, especially if injuries worsen later.

choices.text: Wait until you're fully recovered, weeks later, to contact the platform's support team about medical costs.
choices.feedback: Also a trap. Ride-hailing platforms and insurers generally expect an accident to be reported within a short window (often 24-48 hours) — waiting weeks can be used to deny or delay a claim, even when the accident itself was clearly the platform's driver's fault.

takeaways: Ride-hailing and bike-taxi aggregators are required to carry personal accident cover for riders — but you need documentation (driver name, vehicle number, photos, a police complaint) created at the time of the accident to actually claim it.
Report ride-related accidents through the app's SOS/support within 24 hours — delayed reporting is a common reason claims get denied.
Don't accept an informal cash settlement at the scene, even if it feels faster — it forfeits your ability to claim medical costs later if injuries turn out to be worse than they first appear.

quiz.why: 14 others were injured in the same incident — hill-state tunnel and construction sites face heightened water and debris risk during the monsoon.

quiz.why: The Yellow Line, unaffected today, just crossed its own milestone — 3.7 crore passengers carried in its first year of operation.

quiz.why: The checks have since expanded to put restaurants in Dakshina Kannada district on alert too, with gaps reported from star hotels to quick-commerce warehouses.

quiz.question: The long-running Cauvery water-sharing dispute referenced in this week's Karnataka bandh call is between Karnataka and which other state?
quiz.why: The Cauvery Water Management Authority oversees how much water Karnataka must release downstream to Tamil Nadu, a decades-old flashpoint that still triggers bandh calls today.

quiz.question: In a medical emergency, what is generally considered normal human body temperature in Celsius?
quiz.why: A reading above roughly 38°C (100.4°F) is generally considered a fever — a useful baseline to know before calling 108 for an ambulance.
